brief: The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75%-4.00%, the first increase since July 2023, ending the pause begun in December, on a near-unanimous vote. The new SEP raised the median 2026 rate projection to 4.1%, implying one more hike in 2026 with a cumulative 50bp increase holding through 2027. All but two participants backed two or more 2026 hikes, and eight backed a third by 2027, though UBS says that group skews toward hawkish regional presidents. Inflation forecasts rose despite consensus expecting no change, even as Chair Warsh cited an August core PCE reading of 3.2%, below July's 3.3%, and reiterated that policy is not yet restrictive. He listed inflation trends, activity strength, and geopolitical and commodity developments as the factors behind the hike, plus the share of items with inflation above 3% as a new criterion he is watching. UBS expects another hike in December because the bar to pause is high, but views the market's pricing of four total hikes as excessive, expecting disinflation to weaken the case for further tightening into 2027.
